question:
A company's marginal cost is $MC(x)=4x^3-2x^2+3x+7$.

(a) Set up the definite integral representing additional cost from 1 to 3 units.

(b) Evaluate the integral.

(c) If marginal cost becomes $4x^3-2x^2+3x+7+\sin(\pi x)$, evaluate the revised integral and interpret the result.
explanation:
(a) Additional cost is represented by the definite integral:

$\int_{1}^{3}(4x^3-2x^2+3x+7)dx$.

(b) Antiderivative is $x^4-\frac{2}{3}x^3+\frac{3}{2}x^2+7x$. Evaluating from 1 to 3 gives approximately $88.6667$.

(c) New cost function adds $\sin(\pi x)$. Thus revised integral:

$\int_{1}^{3}(4x^3-2x^2+3x+7+\sin(\pi x))dx$.

$=88.6667+\int_{1}^{3}\sin(\pi x)dx$.

$=88.6667+[-\frac{1}{\pi}\cos(\pi x)]_{1}^{3}$.

Since $\cos3\pi=-1$ and $\cos\pi=-1$, the difference is zero.

Thus the sinusoidal component contributes zero net cost over the interval because positive and negative fluctuations cancel.

options.A:
(a) $\int_0^3(4x^3-2x^2+3x+7)dx$
(b) $108$ approximately
(c) Revised cost is greater because $\sin(\pi x)$ contributes positive net cost
options.B:
(a) $\int_1^3(4x^3-2x^2+3x+7)dx$
(b) $88.6667$ approximately
(c) Revised integral is still $88.6667$ approximately because $\int_1^3\sin(\pi x)dx=0$, so positive and negative fluctuations cancel
options.D:
(a) $\int_1^3\sin(\pi x)dx$
(b) $0$
(c) Revised integral is $0$ because the polynomial part cancels
